correctness.rationale: Semantic equivalence to covering by three coordinate hyperplanes was reconstructed in both directions. A private-selector multilinear-polynomial argument shows every minimal failure has at most eight rows; a four-row pigeonhole cover and explicit five-row witness give the exact lower boundary. Complete C++17 subset enumeration over each size at most eight produced 54, 3672, 36612, 17793 minimal failures, while complete traversal under eight explicit group generators produced 1, 10, 41, 24 orbits. Re-execution reproduces a full canonical 76-class list; an independently written Python neighborhood-union enumerator confirms all 54 size-five obstructions. These finite checks are exhaustive, not extrapolated.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The prior general theorem implies only that finite minimal obstructions are small. It has no mechanism to determine how many ternary three-coordinate obstructions exist, or how they split under the full wreath-product action. The two-atom classification is a distinct lower arity.

value.rationale: The first nonbinary three-constancy-disjunct database/team condition is a canonical 27-assignment finite testbed extending beyond the published two-disjunct setting. Its 76 complete coordinate/value relabeling types and 58,131 explicitly enumerable labelled obstructions provide a reusable finite obstruction library rather than a restatement of generic coherence. The five-row minimum demonstrates genuine domain-size sensitivity and all classes have canonical replayable representatives; their precise numerical values are not implied by the generic multilinear small-witness bound.
